title: Characterization of Volatilized Compounds in Conventional and Organic Vegetable Source Alternative Meat Curing Ingredients
content: Analyzing volatile compounds is crucial in understanding the distinctive flavor and aroma of cured meat products. By examining these compounds, we can gain insights into the sensory characteristics of alternative ingredients and how they contribute to the overall flavor profile of cured meats. In this study, we characterized and quantified the volatile composition of commercially available, conventional, and organically produced pre-converted celery (Apium graveolens) and Swiss chard (Beta vulgaris subsp. maritima) juices and powders used in the meat curing industry. We optimized a method involving steam distillation with liquid-liquid phase extraction coupled with gas chromatog-raphy-tandem mass spectrometry (GC-MS/MS) to isolate and analyze volatile compounds from the vegetable powders and juices. The key volatile compounds identified in celery and Swiss chard were 3-butylisobenzofuran-1(3H)-one and 2-methoxy-4-vinylphenol, re-spectively. In both conventional and organic celery juice, the primary volatile compounds detected were senkyunolide, sedanolide, and limonene, in descending order of concentra-tion. This work lays the groundwork for sensory and volatile compound studies in alter-native meat curing, while also providing more comprehensive information for organic plant and meat producers, processors, and consumers.
